title: Safety Pretraining: Toward the Next Generation of Safe AI
benchmark_measurement: The paper's internal safety scoring mechanism measures the presence of religious content as a factor contributing to how unsafe a piece of text is. Specifically, 'Brief, indirect mentions of political, religious beliefs, or controversial topics' are categorized as 'Slightly Unsafe'. The evaluation also covers the model's propensity to generate harmful content, which can include antisemitic material.
findings: The paper's safety scoring rubric classifies content with 'brief, indirect mentions of... religious beliefs' as slightly unsafe. The proposed safety-pretraining framework was shown to reduce the generation of harmful content, including an example of antisemitic material that glorifies the Holocaust and mentions 'The Jews'. The core finding is that building safety into pretraining is more robust than post-hoc alignment for preventing various types of harmful content, including that which is religiously charged.
